```python
# repository: boltons, file: boltons/debugutils.py
import sys
import time
from reprlib import Repr

def pdb_on_exception(limit=100):
    """Installs a handler which, instead of exiting, attaches a
    post-mortem pdb console whenever an unhandled exception is
    encountered.

    Args:
        limit (int): the max number of stack frames to display when
            printing the traceback

    A similar effect can be achieved from the command-line using the
    following command::

      python -m pdb your_code.py

    But ``pdb_on_exception`` allows you to do this conditionally and within
    your application. To restore default behavior, just do::

      sys.excepthook = sys.__excepthook__
    """
    import pdb
    import sys
    import traceback

    def pdb_excepthook(exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb):
        traceback.print_tb(exc_tb, limit=limit)
        pdb.post_mortem(exc_tb)

    sys.excepthook = pdb_excepthook
    return
```

This means that instead of the program crashing and exiting abruptly, it pauses execution, allowing the developer to examine variables, step through code, and understand what went wrong. The function takes an optional argument `limit`, which determines how many stack frames are shown in the traceback, helping to focus on relevant parts of the call stack. To revert to the normal behavior where exceptions cause the program to exit, developers can restore the original exception handler by setting `sys.excepthook` back to its default value, `sys.__excepthook__`.
